title: A number base converter

milestone.title: Binary: The Language of the Machine

description:
Put the milestone together in one tool. The program reads commands, one per line, until `quit` or the end of the input:

```
bin 77
hex 48879
dec 0x2A
dec 0b1001101
signed 8 11111011
range 16
quit
```

prints

```
77 = 0b1001101
48879 = 0xBEEF
0x2A = 42
0b1001101 = 77
11111011 as signed 8-bit = -5
16 bits: unsigned 0 to 65535, signed -32768 to 32767
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `bin N` | N (decimal, 0 or more) in binary, with `0b` |
| `hex N` | N in upper-case hexadecimal, with `0x` |
| `dec TEXT` | TEXT is binary with `0b`, hexadecimal with `0x` (either case), or plain decimal; prints its decimal value |
| `signed BITS PATTERN` | reads PATTERN (0s and 1s, exactly BITS long) as a two's complement number |
| `range BITS` | the unsigned and signed ranges of that many bits |
| `quit` | stops |

Errors (print one line and carry on):
- an unknown command: `Unknown command: <word>`
- a value that cannot be read: `Not a number: <value>`
- a `signed` pattern whose length is not BITS: `The pattern must have exactly <BITS> bits`

Blank lines are skipped.
hints: One function, `to_base(n, base)`, can do both binary and hex: divide by the base and take digits from `"0123456789ABCDEF"`. Another, `read_digits(text, base)`, can read both, returning `None` when a character is not a digit of that base.

Python beyond the drills: `line.split()` gives the words of a line as a list, and `if not words:` is true when that list is empty. `continue` skips the rest of the loop body and goes on with the next line. `text.lower()` makes text lower case, `ch in "01"` is `True` when `ch` is one of those characters (`not in` is the opposite), and `elif` / `else:` add more branches to an `if`.
requirements: Do the conversions yourself (dividing, doubling and adding), not with `bin`, `hex`, `format` or `int(text, base)`.
Write a function for each conversion, and keep the loop that reads commands short.
rules: Convert to binary yourself instead of using `bin()`.
Convert to hexadecimal yourself instead of using `hex()`.
Read digits yourself instead of `int(text, base)`.

examples.name: the example
examples.stdin:
bin 77
hex 48879
dec 0x2A
dec 0b1001101
signed 8 11111011
range 16
quit

examples.name: edges
examples.stdin:
bin 0
hex 255
dec 0XbeEf
dec 1000
signed 8 01111111
signed 8 10000000
range 8
range 32
examples.expected:
0 = 0b0
255 = 0xFF
0XbeEf = 48879
1000 = 1000
01111111 as signed 8-bit = 127
10000000 as signed 8-bit = -128
8 bits: unsigned 0 to 255, signed -128 to 127
32 bits: unsigned 0 to 4294967295, signed -2147483648 to 2147483647
